text:
alex: Heads-up — saw a weird perf regression on the nightly kv-batch job. tail latency jumped and timeline shows lots of tiny kernels instead of the fused op we expect.

tess: ugh. is this on the new kernel selector change from yesterday?

alex: looks correlated. the selector is choosing the 'micro' variant for many shards. reproducer is the small-seq, small-batch workload on a8.

sam: can you share the nsys capture and flags you used? this sounds like a sampling bias problem where short kernels get undercounted and we miss hot paths.

alex: grabbed a couple of captures. command I used:

```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=nsys_kv_stall --duration=6 --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-sleep=1
```

I also tried a bracketed capture with a 2s warmup, then 3s bracket.

hua: quick note: osrt sampling only picks up kernels above a certain duration cutoff, so a flood of 20-200us kernels looks like a busy timeline but sampling will hide where time is going.

perf-bot: capture uploaded: s3://perf/2331112223/nsys_kv_stall.nsys, flamegraph attached.

alex: flamegraph shows a long flat CPU span with many tiny GPU launches. kernel timeline (nsys) has a huge fan of cudaLaunchKernel events each ~80us. the fused kernel would have reduced launches by ~6x.

sam: couple of experiments to try: 1) increase duration and bracket to catch more steady-state; 2) disable OSRT sampling so nsys records every CUDA call (larger file) or use higher sampling resolution; 3) use NVTX markers around the critical batch path to bracket precisely.

alex: tried disabling sampling: `--sampling=none` (nsys) and did a 12s capture; file was ~1.2GB but kernel timeline was exact. confirmed selector switch is producing more kernel launches at kernel-selection time.

alex: log snippet from the runtime where selector picks micro variant:

```
[2026-03-10T02:14:21Z] selector: stage=kernel_pick batch=8 seq=64 cost_est=12.3 -> picked variant=micro_fwd (est_latency=0.12ms)
[2026-03-10T02:14:21Z] selector: stage=kernel_pick batch=16 seq=64 cost_est=23.6 -> picked variant=fused_fwd (est_latency=0.78ms)
```

hua: that explains it — a small change in cost model weight could push batch=8 into micro_fwd. for our workload batch sizes fluctuate due to batching heuristics, so we end up with many small launches.

tess: actionable: we should 1) add an nsys smoke test that runs with sampling=none and nvtx brackets for the kv path, 2) add a regression alert for average launches/sec exceeding threshold, 3) tweak selector to prefer fused if predicted launches/sec > X.

sam: also recommended to record CUDA memcpy and stream synchronization stalls (in nsys timeline look for cudaMemcpyAsync + stream syncs). sometimes the micro variant introduces extra memcopies.

alex: confirmed extra D2H memcpy in micro path. That plus many launches explains the latency regression.

perf-bot: perf run 2331112223 summary: avg_token_latency +18%, kernel_launch_rate x4, memcpy_bytes_up +42%. Attach: s3://perf/2331112223/summary.json

hua: for the smoke test, here's a minimal capture harness to reproduce reliably:

```
# warmup
python run_perf.py --mode=kv_small --warmup=3
# bracketed capture
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=bracketed_kv --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-end=nvtx --duration=8 --sample=none
```

(we put NVTX begin/end around the critical batching loop)

tess: thanks. I've opened a PR to add the nsys smoke harness and a CI job that keeps an eye on launches/sec.

alex: assigning follow-ups: @sam to add launch-rate alert, @hua to propose selector weight tweak, @tess to land smoke test. I'll own the postmortem blurb for the nightly. :thumbsup:

sam: ack. I'll also run a finer-grained perfetto capture on one machine to get CPU-side syscall timing for launches. might reveal a scheduling hotspot.

hua: one more tip — for inspecting kernel shapes use the kernel name filter in nsys UI and export CSV of durations; helped me spot that the micro kernel had a hidden device-side memcpy.

alex: perfect. thanks everyone, this should get us back to baseline.
